reason: Same defect as CH3-03: torch.profiler's documented capabilities (operator timing, memory, shapes, FLOP estimates) include no active-parameter count; the sentence sends readers to a feature that does not exist, and the reviewer's proposed alternatives (router hook / config parse) are the real methods.
evidence: chapter-03.md:130 verbatim: 'Tools such as `torch.profiler` can count active parameters, but this is an empirical measurement, not a first-party spec.' PyTorch docs (docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/profiler.html, retrieved): profiler options are record_shapes, profile_memory, with_stack, with_flops ('use formula to estimate the FLOPs ... of specific operators (matrix multiplication and 2D convolution)') — no parameter-counting API; the PyTorch profiler recipe describes determining 'the time and memory consumption of the model's operators'.
fix_instruction: File design/manuscript/chapter-03/chapter-03.md, line 130, item 2 'Runtime measurement.' — replace 'Tools such as `torch.profiler` can count active parameters, but this is an empirical measurement, not a first-party spec.' with: 'Infer the count from the execution, e.g. with `torch.profiler` (record_shapes / with_flops) summing the shapes of the matmuls actually run, or a router hook that logs the experts selected per token; this is an empirical measurement, not a first-party spec.' (Same fix as CH3-03; one edit covers both findings.)
